context.guidance: Set up alerting or scheduled review on the access logs and authentication events for every store that holds Personal Data, so unauthorised access is detected and its cause and impact can be established. Rule 6(1)(c) requires monitoring and review of this kind, and investigation depends on it. Make sure the alert rules cover authentication failures and privileged reads, not only application errors.

value.fix: No code change is needed for this line. The evidence is a templated UI or achievement title string ("Solved $difficulties Star Challenges"). It does not access, store or log Personal Data, and it is not a monitoring setting, so it cannot show a MON-01 gap. Mark this finding as a false positive. To actually check MON-01, look at the data stores and auth layer instead, such as the user or customer database, login and session handlers, and admin or privileged read endpoints. Confirm that authentication failures, successful logins, privilege changes and privileged reads of Personal Data are logged in a structured, tamper-resistant form. Those logs should go to a central system with alert rules or a scheduled review covering failed-login spikes, unusual privileged reads and access outside normal patterns, as Rule 6(1)(c) requires.
